subject: Proof points for non-learning SLA and cross-border export constraints
messages:
From: Elle Ramos <elle.ramos@praxishealth.com>

Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 8 Feb 2028 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Request: operational proof for non-learning and export constraints

Hi Hannah,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Our legal team has a couple of detailed asks before we can greenlight a pilot:

- A signed operational attestation that customer interactions will not be used for model training or improvement (no adaptive learning) unless explicitly opted-in.
- Evidence we can rely on for export controls: sample audit logs showing geo-routing and SFTP export mechanics, and confirmation of cross-border transfer safeguards.
- Clarification on prompt/response ownership and whether outputs are considered customer IP or subject to derivative licenses.

I've attached our standard questionnaire (see attachment: praxis-data-serve-qa.xlsx). Can your team supply a concise attestation and any redacted logs we can present internally to PraxisHealth Legal?

We'd like to close this in the next two weeks to hit our Q2 pilot window.

Best,
Elle Ramos
Head of Integrations, PraxisHealth
elle.ramos@praxishealth.com

Attachments: praxis-data-serve-qa.xlsx (questionnaire - see tab "NonLearning")

Hi Elle —

Appreciate the clear list. We're happy to provide the attestations and redacted operational artifacts. Quick clarifications so we tailor what's most useful for PraxisHealth Legal:

1) Do you need a countersigned PDF attestation (signed by Redwood security/ops) or a checklist + on-record email exchange? We can provide both but want to prioritize.
2) For audit log samples, would redacted tenant IDs and truncated request IDs work, or do you require full session traces under an NDA?
3) On prompt/response ownership: is Praxis asking for an explicit IP assignment for generated outputs, or language that confirms customers retain rights to their inputs and outputs (with Redwood retaining derivative rights for model improvements unless excluded)? If you need exclusive assignment we should route to contracts.

I'm attaching a short template that our compliance team uses for non-learning attestations — fills in the runtime controls, KMS residency, and export mechanics.

Next steps: once you confirm answers to the 3 quick questions above I'll loop in Operations to pull a sanitized audit log snippet and coordinate a signed attestation.

Hannah Schmitt

Target: I want a draft attestation and log sample to send to Praxis by EOD Monday (13 Feb). We should avoid exposing raw customer text; redaction and PRX substitution is fine.

Thanks — Hannah

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 13 Feb 2028 07:47:00 -0800
Subject: Re: FW: Request: operational proof for non-learning and export constraints

Hannah — quick responses below; happy to expand if Ops/legal need more detail.

- Runtime enforcement: we have a per-tenant configuration flag (tenant.config.no_training = true/false). It's checked at the API gateway and again validated in the inference worker when requests are enqueued. When set to true, requests are processed with KV write-through disabled and no traces are forwarded to telemetry streams used for model improvement.
- Ephemeral KV: session KV is ephemeral by default and is reclaimed after session TTL; prefix caching is configurable and can be turned off per-tenant. We can document the exact TTL values and the code path where KV reclamation happens.
- Export controls: exports to SFTP are recorded in the export manifest; each manifest row includes export_time, target_host, file_checksum, and exported_by. We can produce a manifest with tenant IDs replaced by PRX-XXXX.

I'll prepare a short ops note with the exact config names and paths and attach a sanitized export-manifest sample.

— Karthik

Attachments: (will attach export-manifest-sample.csv and runtime-flag-reference.md in the follow-up)

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Elle Ramos <elle.ramos@praxishealth.com>, PraxisHealth Legal <legal@praxishealth.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, david_kim@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 12 Feb 2028 14:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: operational proof for non-learning and export constraints

Elle / Praxis Legal team —

Thanks for the patience. Below is a consolidated response and the artifacts you requested. We kept anything that could contain customer content redacted and used practice IDs (PRX-####) to preserve traceability in the sample logs.

1) Attestation (attached): Redwood Inference confirms that, for tenants who opt into the "no_training" configuration, customer interactions are not used for model training or improvement. The attestation includes the enforcement points (API gateway validation, inference worker check, and telemetry gating) and is signed by Redwood's Head of Ops and Director of Privacy. Attachment: redwood-nonlearning-attestation.pdf

2) Audit/log samples: attached audit-log-sample.txt and a sanitized export manifest (export-manifest-sample.csv available on request). Sample entries preserve timestamps and event types; tenant IDs replaced with PRX-XXXX.

3) Prompt/response ownership: By default Redwood's standard DPA language states that customers retain rights to their inputs and generated outputs. Redwood reserves the right to use aggregated, de-identified telemetry for model improvement unless the customer enables the "no_training" configuration or executes a DPA amendment that explicitly excludes such use. If Praxis requires an exclusive assignment or bespoke IP carveout for outputs, we'll need to route that to contracts and may propose a mutually agreeable derivative license in the SOW.

4) Cross-border/export controls: Exports initiated via the customer SFTP connector are logged and retained per our export retention policy (30 days by default, configurable for enterprise agreements). Exports are encrypted in transit (SFTP) and at rest. We can provide a longer retention for the pilot under a contract amendment.

Next steps:
- Please confirm if the attached PDF attestation in its current form is acceptable for Praxis legal sign-off.
- If you need the export-manifest-sample.csv or additional log slices (we have week-long windows available), let us know which date range and we'll produce redacted extracts.
- If Praxis wants to fully exclude Redwood from any derivative rights, indicate that so we can engage Contracts for a DPA addendum.

Thanks — happy to jump on a 30-min call to walk through the artifacts this week.

Hannah Schmitt
Director, Privacy & Trust | Redwood Inference
hannah_schmitt@redwood.com

Attachments: redwood-nonlearning-attestation.pdf (signed attestation), audit-log-sample.txt (sanitized sample)
